metadata.case_name: MAK KAM BO v. EVER GAIN ENGINEERING LTD AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: six cm laceration to the back of the right hand with a fracture of the second metacarpal head.
source: The hospital reports show that Mr Mak suffered a six cm laceration to the back of the right hand with a fracture of the second metacarpal head.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of multiple sites of hand

injuries.description: A second stage operation of osteochondral autograft head of right second metacarpal, using the head of the third metatarsal of the left foot was done on 26 February 2002.
source: A second stage operation of osteochondral autograft head of right second metacarpal, using the head of the third metatarsal of the left foot was done on 26 February 2002.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the wrist or hand

source: He was diagnosed as suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder and depression.
They agreed that he was suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder in relation to the accident and also a depressive reaction in consequence of the accident.

manifestations.description: stiffness in the right index finger
the skin was dark and cold
there was no movement at the joints
could not bend the finger; it stuck out when he made a fist; and it was discoloured
unable to lift more than a catty with his right hand
recurrent numbness and some soreness after walking for half an hour; pain on climbing a ladder
significant fear when exposed to cues that would remind him of the accident
voluntary restriction of motion in bending the index finger

treatments_received: Emergency debridement and extensor tendon repair
osteochondral autograft head of right second metacarpal, using the head of the third metatarsal of the left foot
treatments_future: psychiatric and psychological treatment for two years

losses.description: index finger which will never allow him to do any kind of fine manual work, and will always get in the way of any manual work he has to do.
He obviously cannot return to his pre-accident employment.
significant fear when exposed to cues that would remind him of the accident, as well as other psychological difficulties such as lack of concentration.

He was diagnosed as suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder and depression. They agreed that he was suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder in relation to the accident and also a depressive reaction in consequence of the accident.
